name: Autosomal Recessive Intermediate Charcot-Marie-Tooth Disease Type D

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Electrophysiological Diagnostic Criteria for Charcot-Marie-Tooth Disease

criteria.description: Presence of distal muscle weakness and atrophy predominantly affecting lower limbs
Intermediate nerve conduction velocities (25-45 m/s) on electrophysiological studies
Identification of pathogenic biallelic mutations in genes associated with AR intermediate CMT type D
Consistent autosomal recessive inheritance pattern in family history
Presence of pes cavus or hammer toes

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of distal muscle weakness with intermediate nerve conduction velocities plus genetic confirmation of biallelic pathogenic variants
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Electrophysiological studies are essential to distinguish intermediate CMT from demyelinating or axonal forms.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Distal muscle weakness and atrophy of lower limbs
Intermediate nerve conduction velocity slowing (25-45 m/s)

common.symptomName: Distal sensory loss in lower limbs
searchTerms: loss of feeling in lower feet and legs
reduced sensation in feet and legs

common.symptomName: Reduced or absent deep tendon reflexes
Steppage gait due to foot drop
searchTerms: steppage gait due to foot drop

occasional.symptomName: Mild distal sensory neuropathy in upper limbs
searchTerms: early sensory loss in upper limbs
slight sensory nerve damage in arms

occasional.symptomName: Foot deformities such as hammer toes

imaging: MRI may show muscle atrophy in distal lower limbs
other: Electrophysiological studies showing intermediate slowing of nerve conduction velocities

distinguishingFeatures: Axonal neuropathy with normal or mildly reduced nerve conduction velocities (> 45 m/s)

redFlags: Rapid progression of weakness over weeks
Presence of upper motor neuron signs
references: Pareyson D, Marchesi C. Diagnosis, natural history, and management of Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease. Lancet Neurol. 2009;8(7):654-667.
